links.outcome: Model accuracy, FPR, FNR across race, ethnicity, age, insurance and SES subgroups
links.effect: Black vs non-Hispanic white: accuracy higher (0.051), FPR lower (-0.060), FNR higher (0.049); similar pattern for Hispanic, younger, Medicaid/missing insurance, low SES patients; no consistent c-statistic, ICI or Brier differences.
links.quote: A similar pattern was observed among patients who were Hispanic, younger, with Medicaid/missing insurance, or living in low SES zip codes.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance and fairness metrics on local retrospective data before deployment
links.effect: Subgroup analysis revealed higher FNR and lower FPR for black, Hispanic, younger, Medicaid/missing insurance, and low-SES patients, despite no consistent differences in c-statistic, ICI or Brier Score.
links.quote: An EHR-based mortality risk model was less likely to identify some marginalised patients as potentially benefiting from palliative care, with younger age pinpointed as a possible mechanism.

screen.reason: Retrospective audit/validation of an EHR mortality risk model to evaluate algorithmic bias and equity across demographic and socioeconomic subgroups.
